title: Python: resolveAliasCall resolves C.<attr> to a def when attr is another data descriptor type defines (__dict__, __doc__, __module__, __name__, __qualname__, __bases__, __mro__)
description: GCLI-120 item 2 refuses f = C.__class__; f() to an in-repo def __class__ because type's data descriptor wins over the class body. The rest of that family has the same wrong edge: f = C.__dict__ (and __doc__, __module__, __name__, __qualname__, __bases__, __mro__) with a same-named def in C. Split out per the leader's ruling on the GCLI-120 plan; ordinary, not on the hold list.

acceptanceCriteria.text: f = C.<attr>; f() with in-repo C defining a def, property or attribute of that name resolves no edge to it, for each name in the family, red before and green after
a positive twin where C defines no such name still resolves as before
a mutant that drops the refusal for one name is observed red
